<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module below redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Bound each code with an absolute expiry stored beside its value, and refuse redemption when that time has passed.

`coupon_lookup` currently maps a code to a bare number, so lifetime cannot be enforced no matter what the caller does. The value has to be a record that includes at least:

- the discount amount (what settlement applies)
- `expires_at` (absolute timestamp, set when the code is issued)

Optionally also `not_before` if a code should not be valid immediately.

At redeem time, read that record and apply the amount only if a trusted server clock is within the window (`now >= not_before` and `now < expires_at`). Otherwise treat the code as invalid. Checking only in the issuer, or only in a client, does not make the bound enforceable at lookup.
